name: Quests
description: There are $$$n$$$ quests. If you complete the $$$i$$$-th quest, you will gain $$$a_i$$$ coins. You can only complete at most one quest per day. However, once you complete a quest, you cannot do the same quest again for $$$k$$$ days. (For example, if $$$k=2$$$ and you do quest $$$1$$$ on day $$$1$$$, then you cannot do it on day $$$2$$$ or $$$3$$$, but you can do it again on day $$$4$$$.) You are given two integers $$$c$$$ and $$$d$$$. Find the maximum value of $$$k$$$ such that you can gain at least $$$c$$$ coins over $$$d$$$ days. If no such $$$k$$$ exists, output Impossible . If $$$k$$$ can be arbitrarily large, output Infinity .
input_specification: The input consists of multiple test cases. The first line contains an integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains three integers $$$n,c,d$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 2\cdot10^5$$$; $$$1 \leq c \leq 10^{16}$$$; $$$1 \leq d \leq 2\cdot10^5$$$) — the number of quests, the number of coins you need, and the number of days. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$) — the rewards for the quests. The sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2\cdot10^5$$$, and the sum of $$$d$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2\cdot10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output one of the following. If no such $$$k$$$ exists, output Impossible . If $$$k$$$ can be arbitrarily large, output Infinity . Otherwise, output a single integer — the maximum value of $$$k$$$ such that you can gain at least $$$c$$$ coins over $$$d$$$ days. Please note, the checker is case-sensitive , and you should output strings exactly as they are given.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1760F — Quests [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
